title: Past-Due CHIP Premium Payments by the Family
content:
# Past-Due CHIP Premium Payments by the Family

**Product:** Medicaid Managed Care Membership (Prairie Ridge CHIP Kids family premium account)
**Desk tool:** `pay_past_due_premium_fdc43b6b` (a customer-run tool)

A family on a Medicaid Managed Care Membership that bills a CHIP family premium may pay a coverage month whose due date has passed. The payment is the family's own: it is posted by the family through the payment tool described on this card, for one coverage month, and it settles that coverage month on the premium account.

## What the payment books

One run of the tool posts one payment entry on the membership's premium account:

- the entry is for the coverage month named in the call, carries the amount and the payment method given, and is dated the day it is made;
- the coverage month named is settled: the amount billed for that month leaves the premium balance shown on the membership, whatever amount was paid, and the premium balance never goes below zero;
- the family sees the payment and the settled month on the premium account at once and receives a payment confirmation number.

A coverage month is settled by the payment made for it; the premium balance on the membership falls by the amount billed for that month and by nothing more.

## How it is invoked

`pay_past_due_premium_fdc43b6b` is a hidden tool owned by the customer. The representative unlocks it for the customer and hands it over; the customer themselves then runs it to make the payment. The representative does not run it on the family's behalf.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `membership_id` | The membership reference number of the CHIP membership whose premium is being paid, as returned by the membership lookup and read out by the representative. | Reference number, as shown by the lookup |
| `coverage_month` | The coverage month the payment is for, exactly as the month is labelled on the premium account. | `YYYY-MM`, for example 2026-08 |
| `payment_amount` | The amount paid in USD. | Positive number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent |
| `payment_method` | How the family pays. | Exactly one enum value, below |

Enum values of `payment_method`:

- `online_portal` — paying through the member portal website;
- `phone_ivr` — paying by card or bank draft over the phone payment line;
- `mail_check` — the payment is a mailed personal check;
- `money_order` — the payment is a mailed money order;
- `not_applicable` — no payment method applies, which is never the case for a payment the family makes.

## Return

On success the tool returns a confirmation string of the form:

> Payment <payment_entry_id> posted: <payment_amount> USD for coverage month <coverage_month> on membership <membership_id> by <payment_method>; confirmation number <payment_reference>; premium balance now <premium_balance> USD.

Here `payment_entry_id` is the new premium ledger entry reference (text starting "pay_"), `payment_reference` is the confirmation number (text starting "PRP-"), and `premium_balance` is the membership's remaining premium balance with 2 decimals. A returned confirmation number means the payment is posted.

## Reading the receipt (illustration)

Hypothetical receipt: a membership whose premium balance stood at the billed amount of one month and nothing else. After the family's payment for that month posts, the receipt shows the premium balance now 0.00 USD, because the amount billed for the month has left the balance. Had two months been billed and unpaid, the receipt would show the balance still holding the other month's billed amount, since the payment settles only the month it names.
